solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Question getting drunk by small tree, but still drink

indicators.note: whatever is drunk ends up inside the drinker, so the first item goes inside the second

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
QU is a short form of question
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone at a party has had too much to drink beside a little tree, yet still keeps drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is not about intoxication: the small tree drinks up the question, holding it inside S + ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A squash is a fruit cordial diluted with water, a soft drink with no fizz, hence still.

clue.text: In a stable way with European Community? No doubt about it!

indicators.note: one thing held with another can be carried inside it, so the community abbreviation goes within

parts.note: an exclamation of certainty
standard abbreviation for the European Community

explanation.surface: A political pundit insists the European Community is on a stable footing, beyond any doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a plain joining word, but it signals that the Community abbreviation sits inside the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed securely is held firmly and will not wobble, which is being steady or stable.

clue.text: One carrying coffee or tea service that you must tip

indicators.note: in a down clue the tip is the top, so you sits above the service

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tea service in a café comes with a request to leave the waiter a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as gratuity, but in this down entry it means the top: U is placed above RN.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a large metal container with a tap, used to hold and serve hot coffee or tea.

clue.text: Dismiss dope with no comic material

indicators.note: 'no' takes away the following item from the word before it, leaving only what remains

parts.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job
a clot is a dope, a fool
taken as written
a wit is a comic, someone funny

explanation.surface: A boss sacks an idiot who has no sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking WIT from WITH leaves just H. 'Comic material' looks like a phrase, but material alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth is a coarse woven fabric, as worn in mourning or penitence, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Game clue like this that no-good member's inspired

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so the clue type is taken inside
no-good says the letter standing for good is dropped from the limb

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
this clue is an across clue

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that a sports clue was inspired by one of the team's players.
explanation.walkthrough: G for good leaves LE from LEG, and LE breathes in ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field sport played with netted sticks, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: What might be illustrated by a piece of paper

definitions.text: What might be illustrated by a
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word 'a' is an example of the indefinite one in grammar
second meaning: a written item in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature that comes with pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' looks like it belongs to 'a piece of paper', but it is itself the example: 'a' and 'the' are the articles of English grammar. Paper here means newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite part of speech of that name, and a newspaper story is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Page about two conservatives, one half-cut

indicators.note: cutting something in half removes its second half, keeping only the front part

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the first of the two: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the other one: a Tory is another name for a conservative

explanation.surface: A newspaper page about two Tory politicians, one of whom was rather drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two conservatives' supplies both C and TORY; half-cut means tipsy in Britain, but here only TO of TORY stays.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front side of a leaf.

clue.text: Street cat briefly illuminated by flash motor

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
to cat is a slang verb meaning to vomit or retch
lit means illuminated
a mo, a moment, is a flash of time

explanation.surface: A street cat is caught for a moment in the headlights of a showy car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash motor' wants to be a phrase for the answer, but flash supplies MO. 'Cat' is slang for vomit, giving RETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is British slang for a car, and a stretch limo is an extended luxury car.

clue.text: Excuse time supporting energy-filled Nick Clegg?

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so time comes last
something filled has material put inside it, so the energy goes in

parts.note: Nick Clegg left Parliament, so he is an ex-MP
E is the symbol for energy
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a lively Nick Clegg should be let off his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg, former UK Deputy Prime Minister, lost his seat in 2017, making him an ex-MP; E goes into EXMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a duty is to release them from it, the verb sense of exempt.

clue.text: Capital that's raised then invested in British channel

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so the short phrase sits inside

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something turns it upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
a rut is a channel or groove

explanation.surface: Funds raised for a capital project are put into a British television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a stock way to clue i.e., the abbreviation of Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon.

clue.text: Tories back in charge, vent initially suppressed feeling?

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives

indicators.note: back says the following abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge

indicators.note: suppressing the initial means the first letter is held back and left out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Conservatives return to power and anger is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: 'feeling' here is an adjective, meaning sentient.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscient is a rare word for conscious or aware, so a creature that is feeling, able to sense, is that.

clue.text: Very squeezed by provision of social welfare cut

indicators.note: something squeezed by another is pressed inside it

parts.note: social care is welfare provision
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Government welfare spending is squeezed hard and finally cut.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside CARE, before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut with a knife, as when slicing a joint of meat.

clue.text: I fabricate wheeled motor vehicle on the line?

indicators.note: something wheeled round is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a person who fabricates is a liar
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to making up a wheeled motor vehicle that runs on rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeled motor vehicle' reads as one phrase, but wheeled is the turning signal and vehicle belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled passenger carriage that runs along a railway track.

clue.text: Diligent idiot runs US? That's not entirely correct!

indicators.note: something not correct is wrong, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe that a fool is running America, followed by a half-retraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' suggests losing a letter, but every letter of the fodder is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious and diligent are synonyms, both describing someone who works hard and steadily.

clue.text: Cut cash fund in review — that might show a corporation!

parts.note: to crop is to cut

indicators.note: a review looks back, so the fund is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money

explanation.surface: A company's fund is cut after a financial review, which might expose the corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old jokey slang for a paunch, so the definition is a garment that might show a belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop top is a short shirt ending above the waist, which bares the midriff or stomach.

clue.text: Pro Theresa May? Not at first being Republican

indicators.note: the opening of 'Not' takes the place of the Republican letter

parts.note: a woman leader of the political right
first letter of Not
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Theresa May, a supporter, could ever have been a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May, former Conservative UK Prime Minister, is cryptically a 'lady of the right'; N replaces the R of RIGHT. 'Pro' looks like 'in favour of' but means prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady of the night is a euphemism for a prostitute, and pro is a slang short form of the same.

clue.text: In suggesting the Queen must go down, I cross the line

indicators.note: in a down entry going down moves an item to the bottom, so it is taken from its place and set at the end

parts.note: inferring is used loosely to mean suggesting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A republican protester announces that suggesting the Queen should go is overstepping the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is lifted out of INFERRING and dropped to the foot of the entry. The definition is spoken by the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An infringer is someone who breaks a rule or violates a right, figuratively one who oversteps a boundary.

clue.text: When single chap is arguably sexist in Unison

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
one means single
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A trade unionist complains that a single man getting the job is sexist inside the union Unison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is arguably sexist' is the setter's aside on the phrase, which assumes everyone is a man. Unison is a large British public-service trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one man means everyone acting together at the same moment, an idiom for in unison.

clue.text: Its flowers each developed in a straight line

indicators.note: something developed has grown and changed form, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that each bloom on a plant grew in a neat row.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom measures distance directly from point to point, ignoring roads, as a bird would travel.

clue.text: After getting nothing in, label setters heartless

indicators.note: getting something in means it is put inside, here between the two parts

parts.note: to call something is to label or name it
O looks like zero, nothing
the setters refer to themselves as us

explanation.surface: Someone who has achieved nothing calls crossword setters cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves as 'me' or 'us', a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous and heartless are synonyms, both describing someone unfeeling and cruel to others.

clue.text: Expenditure published: city close to bankruptcy

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
LA, Los Angeles, is a city

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of bankruptcy

explanation.surface: A report reveals a city's spending has brought it to the edge of ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent on something, a synonym for expenditure.

clue.text: Old tax cut one of Corbyn's persuasion achieved

indicators.note: cut means trimmed at the end, losing a final letter

parts.note: scot was a medieval tax, as in scot-free
Jeremy Corbyn, former UK Labour leader, is a socialist, a Red

explanation.surface: An old tax is slashed by a left-winger who has finally got his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot-free' originally meant without paying the scot tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a goal or result is to achieve it, so scored is a synonym for achieved.

clue.text: Impose a restriction on liar involved with TUC

indicators.note: being involved with means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A union body moves to rein in a dishonest member mixed up with the Trades Union Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to cut it short or limit it, the same as restricting it.

clue.text: Top mark the prime minister's picked up … wow!

parts.note: A is the top grade

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: Theresa May was prime minister when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A top grade for the prime minister, and an exclamation of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb: to wow someone is to astonish them.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow someone is to impress and astonish them, which is to amaze them.

clue.text: Potential cereal marketing slogan sounds old hat

indicators.note: sounds says the slogan is heard, not read

parts.note: an ad urging shoppers to sample a cereal

explanation.surface: An advertising catchphrase for breakfast cereal is dismissed as stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a comment on the stale slogan, but it is the literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat of the 18th century, so it is literally an old hat.

clue.text: Spirit and punch both have bishop going kind of red

indicators.note: the bishop going means its abbreviation departs from each word

parts.note: brio is spirit, vivacity
a jab is a quick punch
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Drink and punch at a church party leave the bishop flushed red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'punch' look like drinks, but they are brio and jab, each losing its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish wine region best known for its red wine, so it is a type of red.

clue.text: Certain Protestant ideals gain more ground, Tories ultimately involved

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: last letter of Tories

explanation.surface: A political report says Protestant beliefs are gaining ground, with Conservatives finally taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gain more ground' reads as a phrase, but ground is the mixing signal. Orangeism is the Northern Irish Protestant loyalist movement of the Orange Order.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeism is the creed of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternal body loyal to the British crown.

clue.text: Frozen climber losing heart, cold to the core

indicators.note: going to the core means placed in the very middle
losing heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A mountaineer, frozen and dispirited, is chilled right through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer but is a plant; IVY loses V and C takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something icy is covered in ice or very cold, so it is frozen.

clue.text: Dish out insult number two for Trump in hearing

parts.note: to dis is to insult

indicators.note: in hearing means as it would be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Mike Pence was Donald Trump's vice-president

explanation.surface: Someone hurls insults at Trump's deputy where people can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to give out or distribute, as a pharmacist does with medicine, so to dish out.

clue.text: Colourful children's writer's fish-catching trick

indicators.note: something catching another holds it within

parts.note: a con is a trick
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A children's author is known for a clever trick for landing fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children's writer' suggests an author, but the writer is a drawing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a coloured wax stick that children use for drawing and writing.
